newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia cargo craft space docking fails-Tass.
newsitem.headline: Russia cargo craft space docking fails-Tass.

text.p: An unmanned Russian cargo spacecraft failed on Tuesday to complete a planned docking with the manned orbiting module of the space station Mir, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Tass said two redocking attempts had failed. It quoted a mission control spokesman as saying experts were looking into the reasons for the failures and were deciding whether to make another docking attempt.
The agency said the Progress-M-33 spaceship, in orbit since November 1996, had undocked from Mir on February 6 to make way for a Soyuz TM-25 craft which brought a replacement crew.
The Soyuz brought two Russians and a German cosmonaut back to Earth last Sunday. Russians Vasily Tsibliyev and Alexander Lazutkin and U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger are on Mir at the moment.
It was decided then to redock the Progress because it still had some fuel on board and could help adjust the trajectory of the ageing Mir.
It was the second hitch in just over a week to trouble the 11-year-old Mir, which has already outlived its expected lifespan.
On February 23, a fire broke out on board, forcing the crew to don gas masks.

Russia's space agency is suffering a severe cash crisis which last week prompted it to postpone the launch of its first contribution to a planned international space station, Alpha, which will replace Mir.
